newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ABA sets model for 6th Australian TV channel.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ABA sets model for 6th Australian TV channel.

text.p: The Australian Broadcasting Authority (ABA) said on Wednesday it would propose a joint commercial and community broadcasting model for Australia's sixth television channel.

"The ABA's preferred option is to allow for a commercially viable business which is capable of financing the transmision infrastructure necessary to provide a hih-power, wide coverage signal," ABA Chairman Peter Webb told a cable and satellite television conference.
"This would be in return for a limited number of hours, say two per day or 14 per week, of commercial broadcasting," Webb said.

"Programming provision for the balance of program hours would be the responsibility of a representative, all inclusive community group," he said, adding the group would have a community broadcasting licence.

Australia currently has five television networks, including the Seven Network Ltd, the Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd-owned Nine Network, Canwest Global Communications Corp's Network Ten, and the publicly owned Australian Broadcasting Corp (ABC) and Special Broadcasting Service (SBS).
The ABA's proposal would be sent to Communications Minister Richard Alston by the end of February. Alston would then conduct a review by June 30.
